June · Listen & Shadow 07

The Talk, Slide by Slide — opening, the gap, the design, findings, so what
D O   E N G L I S H   W I T H   B R I A N
PART 1 · OPENING
👤 Audience
How do you make the room care in the first thirty seconds?
첫 30초에 청중을 어떻게 붙잡을 건가요?
make the room care — 청중이 관심 갖게 하다
💬 June
Every year, millions of people sprain an ankle.
해마다 수백만 명이 발목을 삡니다.
sprain — 삐다 · every year — 해마다
같은 패턴으로 — Every year, thousands of athletes drop out. · Every day, hundreds of patients walk in.
💬 June
If you've ever rolled an ankle, you know it happens again.
한 번이라도 삐어보셨다면, 또 삔다는 걸 아실 겁니다.
roll an ankle — 발목을 접질리다
같은 패턴으로 — If you've ever run a marathon, you know the wall. · If you've ever taught, you know that look.
💬 June
Most of us assume an ankle heals and that's the end of it — but it isn't.
흔히들 발목은 나으면 끝이라고 생각하지만, 아닙니다.
assume — 당연히 여기다 · heal — 낫다
같은 패턴으로 — Most of us assume rest is enough — but it isn't. · Most people assume it's simple.
💬 June
The question we started with was simple: what should you train first?
저희가 출발한 질문은 단순했습니다 — 무엇을 먼저 훈련해야 하는가.
the question we started with — 출발 질문
같은 패턴으로 — The question we started with was whether it lasts. · The problem we started with was cost.
PART 2 · THE GAP
👤 Audience
What hadn't been done?
아무도 안 한 일이 뭐였죠?
hadn't been done — 아직 이뤄지지 않았다
💬 June
Previous work has shown that both areas get weaker.
선행 연구에서 두 곳 모두 약해진다는 건 밝혀져 있었습니다.
previous work — 선행 연구 · get weaker — 약해지다
같은 패턴으로 — Previous work has shown a link. · Previous studies have shown the opposite.
💬 June
The two have been studied separately, but never side by side.
다만 둘을 나란히 놓고 본 연구는 없었습니다.
separately — 따로 · side by side — 나란히
같은 패턴으로 — They've been measured separately, but never together. · We ran them side by side.
💬 June
That leaves clinicians guessing about where to start.
그래서 임상가들은 무엇부터 할지 몰랐습니다.
leave someone guessing — 짐작에 맡기다 · clinician — 임상가
같은 패턴으로 — That leaves coaches guessing about load. · It left us guessing about the cause.
💬 June
This is where our study comes in.
저희 연구가 들어가는 지점이 바로 여기입니다.
come in — 끼어들다, 역할을 하다
같은 패턴으로 — This is where the data comes in. · That's where she comes in.
PART 3 · THE DESIGN
👤 Audience
Why twenty-one? Someone will ask.
왜 21명이었죠? 분명히 물어볼 겁니다.
Someone will ask — 누군가 물어볼 것이다
💬 June
We recruited twenty-one participants and assigned them to three groups.
21명을 모집해 세 그룹에 무작위로 배정했습니다.
recruit — 모집하다 · assign — 배정하다
같은 패턴으로 — We recruited thirty and split them in two. · We assigned them at random.
💬 June
The sample size was driven by our pilot data.
표본 수는 예비 연구 결과를 근거로 정했습니다.
sample size — 표본 수 · pilot data — 예비 연구 자료
같은 패턴으로 — The timeline was driven by the semester. · The design was driven by cost.
💬 June
We needed a control group to rule out the training effect itself.
훈련 자체의 효과인지 보려면 대조군이 필요했습니다.
control group — 대조군 · rule out — 배제하다
같은 패턴으로 — We needed a second test to rule out error. · We added a control to rule that out.
💬 June
That's a fair limitation — the sample is small, and we say so.
맞는 지적입니다 — 표본이 작다는 건 저희도 인정합니다.
limitation — 한계 · say so — 그렇게 밝히다
같은 패턴으로 — That's a fair point — we didn't measure that. · That's a fair limitation.
PART 4 · THE FINDINGS
👤 Audience
Both improved. How do you say one is better without overselling it?
둘 다 좋아졌는데, 어떻게 말할 건가요?
oversell — 과하게 말하다
💬 June
Both groups improved, but the difference was in the timing.
두 그룹 다 좋아졌지만, 차이는 시점에 있었습니다.
timing — 시점
같은 패턴으로 — Both worked, but the cost was different. · Both improved, but not at the same rate.
💬 June
The difference showed up at week four.
차이는 4주차에 나타났습니다.
show up — 나타나다
같은 패턴으로 — The effect showed up early. · The problem showed up in the second month.
💬 June
It's a small sample, so I'd be careful reading too much into it.
표본이 작아서 저는 조심스럽게 읽고 있습니다.
read too much into ~ — ~를 과하게 해석하다
같은 패턴으로 — I'd be careful reading too much into one case. · It's early, so I'd be careful.
💬 June
We're not claiming foot core is better — what we can say is it got there sooner.
발 코어가 낫다고 주장하는 게 아니라, 더 빨랐다고 말하는 겁니다.
claim — 주장하다 · get there sooner — 더 빨리 도달하다
같은 패턴으로 — We're not claiming it's a cure — what we can say is it helps. · I'm not saying it's wrong.
PART 5 · SO WHAT
👤 Audience
What should a clinician do differently on Monday?
임상가는 월요일부터 뭘 다르게 해야 하나요?
differently — 다르게
💬 June
What this means in practice is start with the foot.
실제로는 발부터 시작하라는 뜻입니다.
in practice — 실제로는
같은 패턴으로 — What this means in practice is fewer sessions. · In practice, it's about time.
💬 June
That's not to say trunk work doesn't matter — it's about the order.
몸통 훈련이 소용없다는 말은 아닙니다 — 순서의 문제입니다.
That's not to say ~ — ~라는 말은 아니다 · order — 순서
같은 패턴으로 — That's not to say rest is useless. · That's not to say she was wrong.
💬 June
If you take one thing from this talk, it's that the first four weeks matter.
이 강연에서 하나만 가져가신다면, 첫 4주가 중요하다는 것입니다.
take one thing from ~ — ~에서 하나만 가져가다
같은 패턴으로 — If you take one thing from this, it's the timing. · If you remember one number, it's this one.
💬 June
Small, yes — but the effect was consistent.
작은 연구지만, 효과는 일관되게 나타났습니다.
consistent — 일관된
같은 패턴으로 — Small, yes — but it held across the group. · Early, yes — but the direction is clear.
💬 June
Happy to take questions.
질문 받겠습니다.
take questions — 질문을 받다
같은 패턴으로 — Happy to take questions. · I'm happy to go deeper on any of that.
